A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All pages, mathematical content, algorithm displays, Table 1, and end matter support comparison. Neither PDF contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: V1 presents algorithms and mathematical proofs of privacy, correctness, and complexity. Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical, including the revised proofs and end matter. It reports no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the empirical proxy updates, exponential-mechanism sampling, quantile score, sparse-vector selection, and stopping rules. The corrected proxy definition matches the empirical procedure already specified in v1.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or benchmark tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The theoretical private hypothesis-selection setting is unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparisons to BKSW19 and AAAK21; the newly cited works are discussed only as related research.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols appear in either version. The algorithmic sample counts, round budgets, and parameter choices in Algorithm 1 and Section 5.5 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity tests, or empirical case studies. The local proof revisions are theoretical changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, error bars, or significance tests. The concentration arguments and failure-probability guarantees concern theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. After matching Table 1's reordered columns, its approximation factors and sample/time complexity bounds are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 corrects the proxy definition to use empirical semi-distances. Lemma 7.5 changes its second-case threshold and score bound from σ' to σ'/2, introduces separate estimators for the two thresholds, and corrects sample-count notation from t to k. These are local formal revisions; the main theorem guarantees remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and Theorems 2–3 retain the central claim: private hypothesis selection with optimal approximation factor 3, nearly-linear runtime, and polylogarithmic sample complexity, resolving the same previously posed question.

C2.justification: Section 1.2 retains the explanations of privacy-related sample overhead, polynomial dependence on the confidence parameter, and the same two open directions. The substantive mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: The pseudocode procedures, parameter schedules, access model, and computational details are retained. V2 adds no implementation, hardware, code-access, or data-access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Aamand et al. [AAC+24] on finite-domain statistical-computational tradeoffs and Asi et al. [ADH+24] on instance-optimal selection when OPT = 0. These extend the context without redefining the paper's main positioning.

P1.justification: V2 revises proxy notation throughout, makes local prose and proof-exposition edits, updates author/contact text, and adds acknowledgments. The existing technical sections retain their order and overall narrative.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves sample complexity before time complexity and labels the sample count s. Equations and page breaks reflow, while the same comparison table and three algorithm displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves precision by correcting the initial empirical proxy definition and explicitly separating the thresholds needed in Lemma 7.5 and Section 5.1. The added references improve context. The gain is limited: the revised lemma proof retains a closing σ' bound inconsistent with its new σ'/2 statement, leaving the cleanup incomplete. The principal algorithms and guarantees are unchanged.
